lines.text: ## Review recall (step 27, baseline on main d0b7a3c)

`bun run recall <repo-dir> [--prs N | --pr A,B,C] [--json]`: for merged PRs with human inline review comments, the share of comments whose card lookout showed amber/red or with a verified risk line. One comment per thread (the first human one); bots are skipped; file-level comments and lines outside every hunk count as unmapped. Inputs are cached in `~/.cache/lookout/recall/`, model calls in the rank cache: a re-run after a rule change takes seconds. This number replaces the persona gate.
Baseline, the probe repo, 15 most recent merged PRs with human inline comments (33 scanned):
| comments | mapped | pointed | missed | unmapped | recall | top-3 share |
| 33 | 32 (31 on an edited line, 1 on context) | 24 (18 amber, 6 red) | 8 | 1 | **0.75** | 0.75 |

All eight misses are green cards: seven are docs cards (design and workflow documents), one a test card. No miss is a green behaviour card. Open: whether a document that defines behaviour (a plan, a workflow an agent follows) should be amber; a blanket docs rule would buy recall and cost the colour its meaning.

cards.title: Review Recall and Risk Ordering
cards.paragraph: Review cards now mark routine changes in sensitive areas amber rather than red, and reviewers can run `scripts/review-recall.ts` to see whether cards surfaced issues raised in human inline comments. `colorFloor` uses `card.attention === "needs-eyes"` to set red versus amber, `compareCards` ranks attention before skim, and `mapComment` maps comment lines to blocks while `scorePr` counts amber/red cards or verified risk lines as pointed.
cards.risk: The recall score can hide comments that reviewers still need to examine when green documentation or test cards define behaviour, because the baseline counts only amber or red cards and cards with a verified risk line.

cards.title: Configure the local review-recall script
cards.paragraph: The `package.json` `scripts.recall` key adds `bun scripts/review-recall.ts`, which `bun run recall` reads in the local development environment. Undoing this removes the `recall` line.

cards.title: Document the review-recall baseline and its open classification question
cards.paragraph: The `bun run recall <repo-dir> [--prs N | --pr A,B,C] [--json]` section describes how comments are counted and cached, and reports a baseline recall of **0.75** across 33 comments from 15 merged PRs. It says all eight misses were green cards—seven docs cards and one test card—and leaves open whether documents that define behaviour should be amber.
